purpose: Dedicated review of three WTFPL-licensed npm packages that are reached through electron-builder > app-builder-lib > builder-util > sanitize-filename. WTFPL is not OSI-approved. docs/02 requires OSI-approved permissive licenses for the default install, so these packages are admissible only because they are never part of a shipped artifact; this file is the evidence for that claim. It is not an admission of WTFPL for any shipped code.
audited_false_reason: truncate-utf8-bytes 1.0.2 ships no LICENSE file (the manifest is its only license evidence, which policy.md section 1 item 9 calls a hint), and the license field of all three is a WTFPL expression that governance/qa_record.py cannot admit as a default-artifact license. The owner decides; nothing is waived here.
reached_through: pnpm why (2026-11-19): truncate-utf8-bytes > sanitize-filename > builder-util > app-builder-lib / dmg-builder / electron-builder-squirrel-windows / electron-publish > electron-builder (devDependency of @open-ontology/super-ontology-desktop). utf8-byte-length is a dependency of truncate-utf8-bytes. No path from the app's dependencies exists.

packages.name: truncate-utf8-bytes
packages.license_evidence_gap: The published tarball has no LICENSE, COPYING or NOTICE file; the package.json license field (WTFPL) is the only statement. sha256 of the tarball is the digest above.

packages.name: sanitize-filename

obligations: Retain the copyright and permission notice in all copies (applies only if the package were redistributed; it is not).

packages.note: Published 2026-11-07, 11 days before adoption, so it passes the seven-day rule.

obligations: Retain the copyright and permission notice in copies or substantial portions (applies only if redistributed; it is not).

build_time_only_evidence.method: Packed the app with the exact electron-builder.yml (electron-builder --mac dir --arm64, output redirected outside the repository tree), then listed app.asar with @electron/asar.
build_time_only_evidence.result: app.asar contains no sanitize-filename, truncate-utf8-bytes, utf8-byte-length, electron-builder, app-builder-lib, vite, vitest, eslint, typescript or jsdom entry. Its node_modules holds only the production dependency closure of the app (react, react-dom, lucide-react, react-markdown, remark-gfm, intl-messageformat and their runtime dependencies) plus @open-ontology/design-system.
config_reasoning: electron-builder.yml `files` lists electron/**, src/shared/**, resources/bootstrap/**, dist/renderer/**, package.json and three negative globs; extraResources copies only build/oo-bundle (oo, oo-docs-engine, oo-bundle.json) and build/generated/legal.
electron-builder adds node_modules of the app's `dependencies` only; devDependencies (electron-builder and its tree) are never collected.
pnpm licenses list --prod for the app importer (the source of THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) contains none of the three packages.
The prepare scripts (scripts/prepare-oo-bundle.mjs, gen-icon.mjs, gen-notice.mjs) do not copy anything from node_modules into build/.
build_time_only_evidence.caveat: The pack check ran without the oo bundle and legal folder (not built in this tree: electron-builder reported the two sources missing); those two sources do not contain node_modules content. Re-run the same listing on the real DMG's app.asar at release.

owner_flags: WTFPL is permissive but not OSI-approved. These packages are accepted only as build-time tools, on the condition that the DMG never contains them.
truncate-utf8-bytes 1.0.2 has no license file in its tarball; only its manifest says WTFPL.
Replacing electron-builder (or a future builder-util that drops sanitize-filename) removes all three.
